purpose: Additional cases required after runtime inspection of SessionSnapshot contentIdentity, pending EventDefinition storage and journal validation.

developmentPolicy.intermediateBranchBehavior: Explicit CONTENT_CHANGED incompatibility is acceptable during development when documented; do not weaken validation merely to resume old sessions on every intermediate batch.
developmentPolicy.finalRequirement: Final/release T5.1 must register explicit migration routes from supported released source content identities to the final canonical catalog identity.

cases.setup: Session snapshot contentIdentity already equals the active catalog identity.
expected: Resume follows the strict current path without migration.
Snapshot state, pending screen, receipts, journal and RNG remain unchanged except already-supported envelope normalization.
No migration provenance is fabricated.

cases.setup: Legacy completed event has the same string eventId as the new canonical event, but its old title/choices/outcomes differ.
expected: Historical entry remains attributable to the legacy definition via source content identity/event fingerprint.
Saved journal text remains exactly what the player saw.
Validator does not compare the legacy journal against the new canonical definition merely because the ID matches.
No canonical semantic fact beyond an explicitly reviewed equivalence is inferred.

cases.setup: A migrated session contains completed legacy decisions, then continues and records new canonical decisions.
expected: Both legacy and canonical entries validate after subsequent save/resume cycles.
Per-decision provenance disambiguates which definition produced each entry.
Legacy definitions remain excluded from active scheduling.
New canonical decisions use the active catalog definition/fingerprint.

cases.setup: A recognized old session is saved on a pending legacy event whose full EventDefinition is embedded in pendingDecision.
expected: Migration validates the embedded definition against the registered source catalog.
The exact same body, visible/uncertain information, choices, labels and outcomes remain pending.
The pending instanceId is preserved.
Choosing resolves the stored legacy definition without scheduling another event or drawing narrative RNG for reconstruction.
After result lifecycle completion, future scheduling uses only the canonical active catalog.

cases.setup: Pending legacy event has the same eventId as a rewritten canonical event but a different serialized definition.
expected: The new canonical definition is not substituted automatically.
Legacy pending definition remains resolvable if its source catalog is recognized and exact.
Tampered or unrecognized definition fails explicitly.
No new canonical SEEN fact is manufactured unless a reviewed same-scene equivalence allows it.

cases.setup: Migration runtime has access to old event definitions for historical/pending validation.
expected: EventIndex/scheduler candidates contain only active canonical runtime content.
Legacy compatibility definitions cannot be selected by scheduleEvent.
Retired technical IDs can still validate/render old history and resolve an already-presented pending scene.

cases.setup: Resume receives snapshots with current, supported legacy and random/unknown content identities.
expected: Current identity uses no-op fast path.
Supported legacy identity uses the explicit registered migration route.
Unknown identity is rejected with a clear compatibility error.
There is no wildcard old-hash acceptance path.

cases.setup: A supported legacy session migration succeeds in memory but persistence of the next operation fails.
expected: No partially migrated/published session state leaks through a failed commit.
Retry from the same original snapshot produces identical migrated state and RNG.
Migration is deterministic and idempotent.

cases.setup: Two semantic versions share the same eventId across catalog identities.
expected: Compatibility lookup uses source content identity and/or exact event-definition fingerprint, never eventId alone.
Old and new definitions cannot validate as each other.
Historical choice/outcome validation resolves against the producing definition.

cases.setup: A legacy schema/session already contains historical retirement facts produced by pre-T5.1 logic, including v7→v8 early-retirement closure behavior.
expected: Migration does not silently replay history under the corrected future FSM.
Existing closed factual state remains historical truth unless an explicit incompatible-migration policy says otherwise.
Future sessions follow the repaired canonical FSM after migration/continuation where still playable.
Epilogue is not regenerated into a different more-cinematic history solely because terminal logic changed.
